learningObjectives.title: The purpose and value of pilgrimage

questions.q: What is the font in a church used for?
questions.explain: The font holds water for baptism and is often placed near the church entrance to symbolise entry into the Christian community.

questions.q: Which feature of a church is the table where Holy Communion (the Eucharist) is celebrated?
questions.explain: The altar is the focal table on which the bread and wine of the Eucharist are consecrated.

questions.q: What is the raised platform from which a sermon is preached called?
questions.explain: The pulpit is an elevated stand that helps the preacher be seen and heard while delivering the sermon.

questions.q: What is the name of the stand, often shaped like an eagle, from which the Bible is read aloud?
questions.explain: The lectern holds the Bible for public readings and is frequently carved in the form of an eagle.

questions.q: Which part of a church is the main central area where the congregation sits?
questions.explain: The nave is the large central body of the church where worshippers gather during services.

questions.q: Which church in Jerusalem is traditionally believed to stand on the site of Jesus' crucifixion, burial and resurrection?
options: The Church of the Holy Sepulchre
questions.explain: The Church of the Holy Sepulchre marks the traditional site of Calvary and the empty tomb of Jesus.

questions.q: In which country is the pilgrimage site of Lourdes located?
questions.explain: Lourdes is a town in south-western France that became a major Marian pilgrimage centre.

questions.q: Which saint founded the monastery on the island of Iona?
questions.explain: St Columba established a monastery on Iona in the 6th century, from which Christianity spread across Scotland.

questions.q: What is the main difference between a plain cross and a crucifix?
options: A crucifix shows the figure of Jesus on it, while a plain cross does not
A crucifix is only made of wood, while a cross is made of metal
A crucifix is used in baptism, while a cross is not
A crucifix is smaller than a cross
questions.explain: A crucifix bears the body of Christ, emphasising his suffering, whereas an empty cross often emphasises the resurrection.

questions.q: Why were stained glass windows historically valued as a feature in churches?
options: They depicted Bible stories to teach people who could not read
They kept out cold air more effectively than clear glass
They marked the site where pilgrims should kneel
They replaced the need for an altar
questions.explain: Stained glass illustrated scripture and saints, teaching the faith visually in an age when many were illiterate.

questions.q: The iconostasis, a screen covered in holy images, is a distinctive feature of which type of church?
questions.explain: In Orthodox churches the iconostasis of icons separates the sanctuary from the nave and aids devotion.

questions.q: What does the Via Dolorosa in Jerusalem represent for Christian pilgrims?
options: The route Jesus is believed to have walked to his crucifixion
The place where Jesus was baptised
The hill where Jesus gave the Sermon on the Mount
The garden where Jesus ascended to heaven
questions.explain: Pilgrims follow the Via Dolorosa, the 'Way of Sorrows', retracing Jesus' final journey carrying the cross.

questions.q: Why do many pilgrims travel to the spring water at Lourdes?
options: They believe the water can bring healing
They believe it was the site of Jesus' baptism
They wish to be baptised as adults there
They come to see the tomb of St Columba
questions.explain: Following the visions of Mary reported by Bernadette Soubirous, the spring water at Lourdes is associated with healing.

questions.q: The Garden of Gethsemane, visited by pilgrims to Jerusalem, is remembered as the place where Jesus did what?
options: Prayed in anguish before his arrest
questions.explain: Gethsemane is where the Gospels record Jesus praying before he was betrayed and arrested.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes a purpose of Christian pilgrimage?
options: To strengthen faith and grow closer to God
To fulfil a compulsory pillar of the religion
To earn a legal qualification in theology
To replace the need for regular church worship
questions.explain: Pilgrimage is a spiritual journey undertaken to deepen faith, seek renewal and draw nearer to God.

questions.q: How does pilgrimage in Christianity generally differ from Hajj in Islam?
options: Christian pilgrimage is not a compulsory duty for believers
Christian pilgrimage must be done exactly once in a lifetime
Christian pilgrimage can only be made to Rome
Christian pilgrimage is forbidden by the Bible
questions.explain: Unlike the obligatory Hajj, Christian pilgrimage is voluntary and not a required act of the faith.

questions.q: A visitor enters a plain church with no statues, a central pulpit and a large pool at the front for full-immersion baptism. Which tradition is this most likely to be?
questions.explain: Baptist churches typically have simple interiors, prominent pulpits and a pool for adult baptism by full immersion.

questions.q: A Christian who is seriously ill hopes that pilgrimage might bring physical healing. Which site would they most likely choose?
questions.explain: Lourdes is world-famous as a place of hoped-for healing linked to its spring water and reported miracles.

questions.q: A pilgrim wants to walk in the actual footsteps of Jesus' final hours and pray at the site of the empty tomb. Where should they travel?
questions.explain: Jerusalem contains the Via Dolorosa and the Church of the Holy Sepulchre, tracing Jesus' passion and resurrection.

questions.q: A Christian seeks a quiet island of Celtic Christian heritage for reflection and worship in community. Which pilgrimage destination fits best?
questions.explain: Iona, with its ancient abbey and modern ecumenical community, is valued for peaceful retreat and Celtic Christian spirituality.

specSource: Cambridge IGCSE Religious Studies (0490) syllabus; Christianity: Sacred Places & Pilgrimage
